title: A scheme over a field is its fibre at the unique base point
statement: Let $K$ be a field, $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $\xi=(0)$ its unique point. Write $L=\kappa_S(\xi)$ for its scheme residue field [def-weil-residue-field], and let $\varphi:K=\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)\to L$ be the canonical germ map followed by the residue map. Then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of fields, and the canonical morphism $j_\xi:\operatorname{Spec}L\to S$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$, an isomorphism of schemes whose map on global sections, under the affine identifications, is $\varphi$. For every scheme $W$ [def-pc-scheme] and morphism $h:W\to S$, form its scheme-theoretic fibre $F=W_\xi=W\times_S\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $p:F\to W$ and $q:F\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. The projection $p$ is an isomorphism of schemes, $h\circ p=j_\xi\circ q$, and $q=j_\xi^{-1}\circ h\circ p$. These conclusions hold for any choice of the fibre product, with the unique comparison isomorphism commuting with both projections.

proof.text: Use Mathlib Ideal.algEquivResidueFieldOfField at the prime ideal ξ.asIdeal to obtain the canonical algebra equivalence from K to its prime residue field, whose forward map is algebraMap K ξ.asIdeal.ResidueField. This is the field specialization of [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra]: a prime of a field is zero and maximal, and the canonical residue map is injective and surjective.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] with $R=K$ and $\mathfrak p=(0)$. It gives $e:L\xrightarrow{\sim}k_0$ with $\varphi=e^{-1}\circ\pi$ and $j_\xi=\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1}\circ\pi)=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$. Step 1 now makes $\varphi$ an isomorphism. By contravariant functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi^{-1})$ is a two-sided inverse of $j_\xi$: both composites are the spectra of identity field maps. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-global-sections], with $C=K$, $B=L$ and $\psi=\varphi$, identifies the map on global sections of $j_\xi$ with exactly $\varphi$.

proof.text: By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and [def-pc-fibre-product], the chosen fibre is pullback h j with its canonical projections. Mathlib’s pullback.fst instance for an invertible right-hand map gives IsIso p. The pullback condition gives p ≫ h = q ≫ j.hom, and cancellation using j.hom ≫ j.inv = identity gives q = p ≫ h ≫ j.inv. The isomorphism instance is proved by the universal-property inverse lifting (identity, h ≫ j.inv).

source.place: Tags 01K0 (definition-fibre) and 01JP (definition-fibre-product); explicit application of their universal property

proof.text: For any other pullback presentation H, use IsPullback.isIso_fst_of_isIso from [def-pc-fibre-product] to obtain the invertibility of its first projection. H.w gives commutativity and cancellation with j.inv gives the formula for q. The comparison isomorphism is H.isoPullback; its two projection equations are H.isoPullback_hom_fst and H.isoPullback_hom_snd. If another isomorphism has these projection equations, pullback.hom_ext equates the forward morphisms, and Iso.ext equates the isomorphisms.
